## Definitions

- [passage] The intelligent assistant is an AI-powered tool designed for integrated MongoDB development support in MongoDB Compass. It answers natural language questions, assists with debugging errors, and provides guidance for performance optimization. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/compass/query-with-natural-language/compass-ai-assistant.md · keywords: AI-assisted query optimization, query optimization · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/query-with-natural-language/data-explorer-ai-assistant.md

## Structure and components

- [passage] - Text indexes can consume significant RAM. They contain one index entry for each unique stemmed word in each indexed field for each document. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md#storage-requirements-and-performance-costs · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization
- [passage] Text indexes support [`$text`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/text.md#mongodb-query-op.-text) [queries](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/text-search.md#std-label-text-query) on fields that contain string content. They also support [aggregation expressions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-qe-aggregation-operators) for encrypted string fields in [Queryable Encryption](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption.md#std-label-qe-manual-feature-qe) enabled collections. Text indexes improve performance when you search for specific words or strings within string content. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization, $text
- [passage] | Scenario | Performance insight | | --- | --- | | You run a query or aggregation without an index. | Add an index to support the operation. | | You run an aggregation pipeline that uses a [`$lookup`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/lookup.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-lookup) stage. | Embed related data to avoid the need for a `$lookup` operation. | | You run a [`$text`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/text.md#mongodb-query-op.-text) or [`$regex`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#mongodb-query-op.-regex) query. | If possible, use [MongoDB Search](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-search/) to improve performance for text search queries. | | Your database contains too many collections. | Reduce the number of collections. | | Your documents contain an array field with too many elements. | Avoid unbounded arrays. | | The data size of individual documents is too large. | Break up large documents into separate collections. | | Your collection contains too many indexes. | Review your indexes and remove any that are unnecessary. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-ui/performance-insights.md#behavior · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization, $lookup, $text, $regex
- [passage] This example matches documents where `runtime` is greater than `1000` and the indexed fields contain `baseball` or `colorado`. It sorts by ascending `year`, then descending relevance score: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/text.md#combine-text-with-other-query-and-sort-operations · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, runtime, 1000, baseball, colorado
- [passage] If the `movies` collection contains an index `{ year: 1, title: 1 }`, the following pipeline can use that index to find the first document of each group: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/group.md#optimization-to-return-the-first-or-last-document-of-each-group · keywords: index, query optimization, movies, { year: 1, title: 1 }
- [passage] 1. The `movies` collection contains documents where the `metacritic` field is present in some documents and absent from others. Of the 21,349 documents, 6,964 have the `metacritic` field and 14,385 do not. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists.md#use-a-sparse-index-to-improve-exists-performance · keywords: index, query optimization, movies, metacritic
- [passage] For example, a pipeline that consists of [`$match`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/match.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-match), [`$sort`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sort.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-sort), [`$group`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/group.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-group) can benefit from indexes at every stage: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-optimization.md#indexes · keywords: index, query optimization, $match, $sort, $group
- [passage] Because the index contains all fields required by the query, MongoDB can both match the [query conditions](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-documents.md#std-label-read-operations-query-document) and return the results using only the index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md#performance · keywords: index, query optimization
- [passage] Contains information on the selection of the query plan by the [query optimizer.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-read-operations-query-optimization) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: index, query optimization
- [passage] | Field | Description | Applicable Stages | | --- | --- | --- | | `docsExamined` | Specifies the number of documents scanned during the query execution stage. | `COLLSCAN`, `FETCH` | | `keysExamined` | For query execution stages that scan an index `keysExamined` is the total number of in-bounds and out-of-bounds keys that are examined in the process of the index scan. If the index scan consists of a single contiguous range of keys, only in-bounds keys need to be examined. If the index bounds consists of several key ranges, the index scan execution process may examine out-of-bounds keys in order to skip from the end of one range to the beginning of the next. | `IXSCAN` | | `numReads` | The number of documents scanned or index keys examined during the query execution stage. **New in version 5.1** | `COLLSCAN`, `IXSCAN` | | `seeks` | The number of times that we had to seek the index cursor to a new position in order to complete the index scan. | `IXSCAN` | | `usedDisk` | Whether the stage wrote to disk. **New in version 5.3** | `GROUP` | | `spills` | The number of times the stage spilled to disk. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledBytes` | The total amount of data written to disk in bytes. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledRecords` | The total number of individual records spilled to disk. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `spilledDataStorageSize` | The total disk space, in bytes, used by the spilled data. **New in version 8.2** | `GROUP`, `SORT` | | `peakTrackedMemBytes` | **New in version 8.3** Maximum number of bytes of tracked memory in use by the current query operation. Starting in MongoDB 9.0, the `COUNT_SCAN`, `GEO_NEAR_2D`, `GEO_NEAR_2DSPHERE`, and `UPDATE` stages also report this field. | `COUNT_SCAN`, `GEO_NEAR_2D`, `GEO_NEAR_2DSPHERE`, `GROUP`, `SORT`, `UPDATE` | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: index, release notes, docsExamined, COLLSCAN, FETCH, keysExamined
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 9.0, when you run `explain` in a mimumum of [executionStats](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.explain.md#std-label-explain-method-executionStats) verbosity mode, aggregation stages that use the classic query execution engine output a `expressionEvaluationPeakMemoryBytes` field. This field contains the peak memory usage, in bytes, from expression evaluation during stage execution. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#aggregation-stages-with-expression-memory-tracking · keywords: index, release notes, explain, expressionEvaluationPeakMemoryBytes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/

## How it works

- [passage] - When building large text indexes, ensure sufficient file descriptor limits. See [recommended settings.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/ulimit.md#std-label-ulimit) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md#storage-requirements-and-performance-costs · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization
- [passage] - Text indexes store individual words, not multi-word strings or word proximity information. Queries with multiple words run faster when the entire collection fits in RAM. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md#storage-requirements-and-performance-costs · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization
- [passage] When explain is run in either executionStats or allPlansExecution verbosity mode, certain aggregation stages that may spill to disk have additional output. These stages include $sort, $group, $setWindowFields, $bucketAuto, $graphLookup, and $lookup (when using the slot-based execution engine). Starting in MongoDB 8.1, this also includes $text queries that use the TextOr execution stage. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, release notes
- [passage] Text indexes support `$text` queries on fields containing string content. Text indexes improve performance when searching for specific words or multi-word strings within string content. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/create-text-index.md · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization, $text
- [passage] - A sort on `{ <timeField>: ±1 }` uses a secondary index on `{ metaField: ±1, timeField: ±1 }` when there is a point predicate on `<metaField>`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-secondary-index.md#use-secondary-indexes-to-improve-sort-performance · keywords: index, query optimization, { <timeField>: ±1 }, { metaField: ±1, timeField: ±1 }, <metaField>
- [passage] Last point queries are most performant when they use the [DISTINCT\_SCAN optimization](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-explain-results). This optimization is only available when an index on `timeField` is descending. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-secondary-index.md#last-point-queries-on-time-series-collections · keywords: index, query optimization, timeField
- [passage] Index hints cause MongoDB to use a specific index for a query. Some operations on time series collections can only take advantage of an index if that index is specified in a hint. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-secondary-index.md#specify-index-hints-for-time-series-collections · keywords: index, query optimization
- [passage] For example, the following query causes MongoDB to use the `timestamp_1_metadata.sensorId_1` index: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-secondary-index.md#specify-index-hints-for-time-series-collections · keywords: index, query optimization, timestamp_1_metadata.sensorId_1
- [passage] - [`executionStats.totalKeysExamined`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.executionStats.totalKeysExamined) displays `3809` to indicate that MongoDB scanned 3,809 index entries. The number of keys examined match the number of documents returned, meaning that the [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) only had to examine index keys to return the results. The [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) did not have to scan all of the documents, and only the 3,809 matching documents had to be pulled into memory. This results in a very efficient query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: index, query optimization, executionStats.totalKeysExamined, 3809, mongod
- [passage] When run with an index, the query scans only as many index entries and documents as it returns, resulting in a more efficient query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: index, query optimization
- [passage] - When possible, put [`$match`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/match.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-match) at the beginning of the pipeline to use indexes that scan the matching documents in a collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-optimization.md#document-filters · keywords: index, query optimization, $match

## How-to and procedures

- [passage] To optimize your indexes, we recommend deploying [dedicated Search nodes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cluster-config/multi-cloud-distribution.md#std-label-configure-search-nodes), which allows you to scale your Atlas cluster and [`$search`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/query/aggregation-stages/search.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-search) workloads independently. Dedicated Search Nodes only run the `mongot` process and therefore improve the availability, performance, and workload balancing of the `mongot` process. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md#implement-a-long-term-solution · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization, $search, mongot
- [passage] To improve query performance, you can create a [compound text index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/create-text-index.md#std-label-compound-text-index-example) and include an equality match in your `$text` queries. If the compound index contains the field used in your equality match, the index scans fewer entries and returns results faster. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/limit-number-of-items-scanned-for-text-search.md · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization, $text
- [passage] Create a secondary single-field index on the `timestamp` field: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-secondary-index.md#use-secondary-indexes-to-improve-sort-performance · keywords: index, query optimization, timestamp
- [passage] To confirm that the sort operation used the Secondary Index, run the operation again with the `explain` option: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-secondary-index.md#use-secondary-indexes-to-improve-sort-performance · keywords: index, query optimization, explain
- [passage] To confirm that the last point query used the secondary index, run the operation again using `explain`: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-secondary-index.md#last-point-queries-on-time-series-collections · keywords: index, query optimization, explain
- [passage] To confirm that the sort operation used the Secondary Index, run the operation again with the `.explain( "executionStats" )` option: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-secondary-index.md#use-secondary-indexes-to-improve-sort-performance · keywords: index, query optimization, .explain( "executionStats" )
- [passage] To confirm that the last point query used the secondary index, run the operation again using `.explain( "executionStats" )`: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries/timeseries-secondary-index.md#last-point-queries-on-time-series-collections · keywords: index, query optimization, .explain( "executionStats" )
- [passage] To view the query plan selected, chain the [`cursor.explain("executionStats")`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) cursor method to the end of the **find** command: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: index, query optimization, cursor.explain("executionStats")
- [passage] To support the query on the `year` field, add an index on the `year` field: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: index, query optimization, year
- [passage] To view the query plan statistics, use the [`explain()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.explain.md#mongodb-method-cursor.explain) method: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: index, query optimization, explain()
- [passage] To support the query, add a [compound index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-compound.md#std-label-index-type-compound). With compound indexes, the order of the fields matter. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: index, query optimization
- [passage] To determine whether a pipeline uses indexes, review the query plan and look for `IXSCAN` or `DISTINCT_SCAN` plans. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-optimization.md#indexes · keywords: index, query optimization, IXSCAN, DISTINCT_SCAN

## Measurements and reference values

- [passage] This alert might appear when Atlas automatically [upgrades your search indexes](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/performance/index-performance.md#std-label-index-create-and-update) to enable new features. Your cluster must have sufficient disk space for both the previous and new version of the index. If the rebuild increases disk space use to 90% or more, Atlas increases the cluster storage if you enabled auto-scaling. After the index upgrade completes, Atlas deletes the old version of the index, which frees up disk space. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md#alert-conditions · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [passage] | Text Index | MongoDB Search Index | | --- | --- | | `db.movies.aggregate([ { $match: { year: {$gte: 2000, $lte: 2010}, $text: { $search: "poet" }, genres : { $eq: "Comedy" } } }, { "$sort": { "year": 1 } }, { "$limit": 3 }, { "$project": { "_id": 0, "title": 1, "genres": 1, "plot": 1, "year": 1 }, — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/recommend-search-text.md#improve-performance-of-queries-using-mongodb-search · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization
- [fact] Other $text restrictions: a query with $text cannot use hint(); text indexes do not improve sort performance; a multi-word phrase mixed with single terms matches only documents containing the full phrase; text indexes accept only binary comparison, so a collection with a non-simple collation needs collation {locale: 'simple'} on the text index; compound text indexes need equality conditions on key prefixes. — https://mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/text-index-restrictions/ · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization, Atlas Search vs $text vs $regex (search offload decision)
- [passage] WARNING: If you shard a collection that already has a MongoDB Search index, you might experience a brief period of incomplete search results while the index is building on a shard. Also, if you add a shard for an already sharded collection that contains a MongoDB Search index, your search queries against that collection might return incomplete results until the initial sync process completes on the added shards. To learn more, see [initial sync process.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/performance/index-performance.md#std-label-troubleshoot-initial-sync) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization
- [passage] Text indexes cannot improve performance for sort operations. This restriction applies to both single-field and compound text indexes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/text-index-restrictions.md#text-index-and-sort · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization
- [passage] In a small collection like the one used in the preceding example, there isn't a noticeable difference in performance between single-field and compound text indexes. However, in larger collections, increased index entry scans can noticeably hinder performance. For best performance, create text indexes that limit the number of index entries scanned to best fit your equality matches. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/limit-number-of-items-scanned-for-text-search.md#view-number-of-documents-examined · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization
- [passage] Case-insensitive indexes do not improve performance for [`$regex`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#mongodb-query-op.-regex) queries, as the `$regex` operator is not collation-aware and therefore cannot take advantage of such indexes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#case-insensitive-queries · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization, $regex · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-case-insensitive.md
- [fact] In 9.0 the classic engine reports expressionEvaluationPeakMemoryBytes in explain at executionStats verbosity or higher for $project, $addFields, $set, $unset, $replaceRoot, $replaceWith, $match, $bucketAuto, $graphLookup and $lookup. A failed operation logs 'Query exceeded the memory limit' with code 12932700. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/9.0/ · keywords: index, release notes, Post-8.0 Query Engine Changes (8.1 and 8.2 rapid releases and 9.0)
- [passage] | Status | Description | | --- | --- | | `BUILDING` | The following scenarios can cause an index to be in the `BUILDING` state: MongoDB is building the index or re-building the index after an edit.; MongoDB Search cannot keep up with indexing changes to the collection. In this case, Atlas rebuilds the index in the background. When the index is in the `BUILDING` state: For a new index, MongoDB Search cannot use the index for queries until the index build is complete.; For an existing index, MongoDB Search uses the old index definition for queries until the index rebuild is complete. An index in the `BUILDING` state may be queryable or non-queryable. | | `DOES_NOT_EXIST` | The index does not exist. An index in the `DOES_NOT_EXIST` state is always non-queryable. | | `DELETING` | MongoDB is deleting the index. An index in the `DELETING` state is always non-queryable. | | `FAILED` | The index build failed. Indexes can enter the `FAILED` state due to an invalid index definition. An index in the `FAILED` state may be queryable or non-queryable. | | `PENDING` | MongoDB has not yet started building the index. An index in the `PENDING` state is always non-queryable. | | `READY` | The index is ready and can support queries. An index in the `READY` state is always queryable. | | `STALE` | The index is queryable but has stopped replicating data from the indexed collection. Searches on the index may return out-of-date data. Indexes can enter the `STALE` state due to replication errors. An index in the `STALE` state is always queryable. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/listSearchIndexes.md#mongodb-search-index-statuses · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, BUILDING, DOES_NOT_EXIST, DELETING, FAILED
- [fact] A case-sensitive $regex can use an index range scan only when the pattern is an anchored simple prefix (starts with ^ or \A followed by simple characters); the scan stops once the prefix no longer matches. Unanchored patterns and patterns with leading wildcards cannot narrow the index range. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/current/reference/operator/query/regex/ · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, Atlas Search vs $text vs $regex (search offload decision)
- [passage] | `$exists` Query | Using a Sparse Index | Using a Non-Sparse Index | | --- | --- | --- | | `{ $exists: true }` | Most efficient. MongoDB can make an exact match and does not require a `FETCH`. | More efficient than queries without an index, but still requires a `FETCH`. | | `{ $exists: false }` | Cannot use the index and requires a `COLLSCAN`. | Requires a `FETCH`. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/exists.md#use-a-sparse-index-to-improve-exists-performance · keywords: index, query optimization, $exists, { $exists: true }, FETCH, { $exists: false }
- [passage] - Use the [`$match`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/match.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-match), [`$limit`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/limit.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-limit), and [`$skip`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/skip.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-skip) stages to restrict the documents that enter the pipeline. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-optimization.md#document-filters · keywords: index, query optimization, $match, $limit, $skip
- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `distanceField` | string | The output field that contains the calculated distance. To specify a field within an embedded document, use [dot notation.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-dot-notation) This field is required for queries on timeseries collections. Starting in MongoDB 8.1, `distanceField` is optional for queries on non-timeseries collections. | | `distanceMultiplier` | number | Optional. The factor to multiply all distances returned by the query. For example, use the `distanceMultiplier` to convert radians, as returned by a spherical query, to kilometers by multiplying by the radius of the Earth. | | `includeLocs` | string | Optional. This specifies the output field that identifies the location used to calculate the distance. This option is useful when a location field contains multiple locations. To specify a field within an embedded document, use [dot notation.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-dot-notation) | | `key` | | Optional. Specify the geospatial indexed field to use when calculating the distance. If your collection has multiple `2d` and/or multiple `2dsphere` indexes, you **must** use the `key` option to specify the indexed field path to use. [Specify Which Geospatial Index to Use](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geonear.md#std-label-pipeline-geoNear-key-param-example) provides a full example. If there is more than one `2d` index or more than one `2dsphere` index and you do not specify a `key`, MongoDB will return an error. If you do not specify the `key`, and you have at most only one `2d` index and/or only one `2dsphere` index, MongoDB looks first for a `2d` index to use. If a `2d` index does not exists, then MongoDB looks for a `2dsphere` index to use. You must specify the `key` field for `$geoNear` on a time series collection. | | `maxDistance` | number | Optional. The maximum distance from the center point that the documents *can* be. MongoDB limits the results to those documents that fall within the specified distance from the center point. Starting in version 7.2, you can specify a valid constant [expression](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-aggregation-expressions) that resolves to a number. Specify the distance in meters if the specified point is [GeoJSON](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-GeoJSON) and in radians if the specified point is [legacy coordinate pairs.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-legacy-coordinate-pairs) | | `minDistance` | number | Optional. The minimum distance from the center point that the documents *can* be. MongoDB limits the results to those documents that fall outside the specified distance from the center point. Starting in version 7.2, you can specify a valid constant [expression](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/mql/expressions.md#std-label-aggregation-expressions) that resolves to a number. Specify the distance in meters for GeoJSON data and in radians for legacy coordinate pairs. | | `near` | GeoJSON point or [legacy coordinate pair](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-legacy-coordinate-pairs) | The point for which to find the closest documents. If using a [2dsphere](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2dsphere.md#std-label-2dsphere-index) index, you can specify the point as either a GeoJSON point or legacy coordinate pair. If using a [2d](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2d.md#std-label-2d-index) index, specify the point as a legacy coordinate pair. | | `query` | document | Optional. Limits the results to the documents that match the query. The query syntax is the usual MongoDB [read operation query](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/query-documents.md#std-label-read-operations-query-argument) syntax. You cannot specify a [`$near`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/near.md#mongodb-query-op.-near) predicate in the `query` field of the `$geoNear` stage. You can't use the `query` field for `$geoNear` on a [time series collection.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/timeseries-collections.md#std-label-manual-timeseries-landing) | | `spherical` | boolean | Optional. Determines how MongoDB calculates the distance between two points: When `true`, MongoDB uses [`$nearSphere`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/nearsphere.md#mongodb-query-op.-nearSphere) semantics and calculates distances using spherical geometry.; When `false`, MongoDB uses [`$near`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/near.md#mongodb-query-op.-near) semantics: spherical geometry for [2dsphere](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2dsphere.md#std-label-2dsphere-index) indexes and planar geometry for [2d](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2d.md#std-label-2d-index) indexes. *Default: false.* | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/geoNear.md#definition · keywords: index, release notes, distanceField, distanceMultiplier, includeLocs, key
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 9.0, if an indexed field becomes a multikey field while a query that references the field is running, the query might fail with a QueryKilledError. An indexed field becomes multikey when you insert or update a document so the field contains an array value. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/ · keywords: index, release notes · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/create-multikey-index-basic.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey/create-multikey-index-embedded.md
- [passage] | Field | Description | | --- | --- | | [into](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-into) | The output collection. Specify either: The collection name as a string to output to a collection in the same database where the aggregation is run. For example:`into: "myOutput"`; The database and collection name in a document to output to a collection in the specified database. For example:`into: { db:"myDB", coll:"myOutput" }` If the output collection does not exist, `$merge` creates the collection: For a [replica set](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/replication.md#std-label-replica-set) or a standalone, if the output database does not exist, `$merge` also creates the database.; For a [sharded cluster](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/sharding.md#std-label-sharded-cluster), the specified output database must already exist. The output collection can be a sharded collection. | | [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) | Optional. Field or fields that act as a unique identifier for a document. The identifier determines if a results document [matches](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched) an existing document in the output collection. Specify either: A single field name as a string. For example:`on: "_id"`; A combination of fields in an array. For example:`on: [ "date", "customerId" ]`The order of the fields in the array does not matter, and you cannot specify the same field multiple times. For the specified field or fields: The aggregation results documents must contain the field(s) specified in the `on`, unless the `on` field is the `_id` field. If the `_id` field is missing from a results document, MongoDB adds it automatically.; For deployments running MongoDB 8.0 and earlier, specified field or fields for `on` cannot be missing or contain a null value. Starting in MongoDB 8.1, if the [supporting index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on-supporting-index) is not sparse, the specified field or fields for `on` can be missing or contain a null value.; The specified field or fields cannot contain an array value. `$merge` requires a [unique](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#std-label-index-type-unique) index with keys that correspond to the [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) identifier fields. Although the order of the index key specification does not matter, the unique index must only contain the `on` fields as its keys. The index must also have the same [collation](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/collation.md#std-label-collation) as the aggregation's collation.; The unique index can be a [sparse](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-sparse.md#std-label-index-type-sparse) index.; The unique index cannot be a [partial](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-partial.md#std-label-index-type-partial) index.; For output collections that already exist, the corresponding index must already exist. The default value for [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) depends on the output collection: If the output collection does not exist, the [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) identifier must be and defaults to the `_id` field. The corresponding unique `_id` index is automatically created.To use a different [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) identifier field(s) for a collection that does not exist, you can create the collection first by creating a unique index on the desired field(s). See the [section on non-existent output collection](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-use-different-on) for an example.; Starting in MongoDB 8.3, the server checks to ensure that the automatically created `_id` index matches the query's collation. If the collations do not match, the `_id` index cannot provide uniqueness for the query, and the query will not run.; If the existing output collection is unsharded, the `on` identifier defaults to the `_id` field.; If the existing output collection is a sharded collection, the [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) identifier defaults to all the shard key fields and the `_id` field. If specifying a different `on` identifier, the `on` must contain all the shard key fields. | | [whenMatched](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched) | Optional. The behavior of `$merge` if a result document and an existing document in the collection have the same value for the specified [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) field(s). You can specify either: One of the pre-defined action strings:["replace":](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched-replace)Replace the existing document in the [output collection](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-into) with the matching results document.When performing a replace, the replacement document cannot result in a modification of the `_id` value or, if the output collection is sharded, the shard key value. Otherwise, the operation generates an error.To avoid this error, if the [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) field does not include the `_id` field, remove the `_id` field in the aggregation results to avoid the error, such as with a preceding [`$unset`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unset.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-unset) stage, and so on.; ["keepExisting":](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched-keepExisting)Keep the existing document in the [output collection.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-into); ["merge"](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched-merge) (Default):Merge the matching documents (similar to the [`$mergeObjects`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/expression/mergeobjects.md#mongodb-expression-exp.-mergeObjects) operator).If the results document contains fields not in the existing document, add these new fields to the existing document.; If the results document contains fields in the existing document, replace the existing field values with those from the results document.For example, if the output collection has the document:`{ _id: 1, a: 1, b: 1 }`And the aggregation results has the document:`{ _id: 1, b: 5, z: 1 }`Then, the merged document is:`{ _id: 1, a: 1, b: 5, z: 1 }`When performing a merge, the merged document cannot result in a modification of the `_id` value or, if the output collection is sharded, the shard key value. Otherwise, the operation generates an error.To avoid this error, if the [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) field does not include the `_id` field, remove the `_id` field in the aggregation results to avoid the error, such as with a preceding [`$unset`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unset.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-unset) stage, and so on.; ["fail":](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched-fail)Stop and fail the aggregation operation. Any changes to the output collection from previous documents are not reverted.; An aggregation pipeline to update the document in the collection.`[ <stage1>, <stage2> ... ]`The pipeline can only consist of the following stages:[`$addFields`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/addfields.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-addFields) and its alias [`$set`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/set.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-set); [`$project`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/project.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-project) and its alias [`$unset`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/unset.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-unset); [`$replaceRoot`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/replaceroot.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-replaceRoot) and its alias [`$replaceWith`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/replacewith.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-replaceWith)The pipeline cannot modify the [on](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-on) field's value. For example, if you are matching on the field `month`, the pipeline cannot modify the `month` field.The whenMatched `pipeline` can directly access the fields of the existing documents in the **output** collection using `$<field>`.To access the fields from the aggregation results documents, use either:The built-in `$$new` variable to access the field. Specifically, `$$new.<field>`. The `$$new` variable is only available if the [let](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-let) specification is omitted.; The user-defined variables in the [let](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-let) field.Specify the double dollar sign ($$) prefix together with the variable name in the form `$$<variable_name>`. For example, `$$year`. If the variable is set to a document, you can also include a document field in the form `$$<variable_name>.<field>`. For example, `$$year.month`.For more examples, see [Use Variables to Customize the Merge.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-variables-example) | | [let](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-let) | Optional. Specifies variables for use in the [whenMatched pipeline.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched-pipeline) Specify a document with the variable names and value expressions: `{ <variable_name_1>: <expression_1>, ..., <variable_name_n>: <expression_n> }` If unspecified, defaults to `{ new: "$$ROOT" }` (see [`ROOT`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/aggregation-variables.md#mongodb-variable-variable.ROOT)). The [whenMatched pipeline](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched-pipeline) can access the `$$new` variable. To access the variables in the [whenMatched pipeline:](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenMatched-pipeline) Specify the double dollar sign ($$) prefix together with the variable name in the form `$$<variable_name>`. For example, `$$year`. If the variable is set to a document, you can also include a document field in the form `$$<variable_name>.<field>`. For example, `$$year.month`. For examples, see [Use Variables to Customize the Merge.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-variables-example) | | [whenNotMatched](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenNotMatched) | Optional. The behavior of `$merge` if a result document does not match an existing document in the out collection. You can specify one of the pre-defined action strings: ["insert"](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenNotMatched-insert) (Default):Insert the document into the output collection.; ["discard":](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenNotMatched-discard)Discard the document. Specifically, `$merge` does not insert the document into the output collection.; ["fail":](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#std-label-merge-whenNotMatched-fail)Stop and fail the aggregation operation. Any changes already written to the output collection are not reverted. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/merge.md#syntax · keywords: index, release notes, into: "myOutput", into: { db:"myDB", coll:"myOutput" }, $merge, on: "_id"

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [passage] - [MongoDB Search](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-search/) provides improved performance and functionality compared to on-premises text search. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types.md#text-index · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization
- [passage] A compound text index on the `department` and `description` fields limits the index keys scanned to only documents within the specified `department`. The compound text index provides improved performance compared to a single-field text index on the `description` field. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/limit-number-of-items-scanned-for-text-search.md#about-this-task · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization, department, description
- [fact] MongoDB's 9.0 performance claims versus 8.0: up to 35% faster find-one, 30% faster update-one, 20% higher transactional throughput, nearly 2x throughput on large deployments. The vendor says these come from internal testing and vary by workload. Percona could not find methodology or raw data, and press coverage reports no benchmark configuration. — https://mongodb.com/company/blog/product-release-announcements/mongodb-9-0-this-is-what-a-database-should-be · keywords: query optimization, release notes, Post-8.0 Query Engine Changes (8.1 and 8.2 rapid releases and 9.0)
- [statement] 8.2.0 known issues: up to 15% change-stream performance degradation versus 8.0, and a $group distinct-scan-on-sparse-index bug that hides null/missing results (SERVER-110423) fixed in 8.2.2. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/8.2 · keywords: query optimization, release notes, Post-8.0 Query Engine Changes (8.1 and 8.2 rapid releases and 9.0)
- [passage] To drop a [text](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md#std-label-index-type-text) index, specify the index name instead of the index specification document. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/dropIndexes.md#text-indexes · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropIndexes.md
- [passage] The second compound index, `{ rated: 1, year: 1 }`, is therefore the more efficient index for supporting the example query, as the MongoDB server only needs to scan `235` [`index keys`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#mongodb-data-explain.executionStats.totalKeysExamined) to find all matching documents using this index, compared to `246` when using the compound index `{ year: 1, rated: 1 }`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/analyze-query-plan.md#mongodb-shell · keywords: index, query optimization, { rated: 1, year: 1 }, 235, index keys, 246

## Facts and statements

- [passage] - Building a text index is similar to building a large [multikey index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-multikey.md#std-label-index-type-multi-key) but takes longer than building an ordered (scalar) index on the same data. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text.md#storage-requirements-and-performance-costs · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization
- [passage] > Derived 2026-10-19; topic-filtered subset of mongodb.com-docs-query.md: Server manual pages about queries, indexes, aggregation, time series, profiling, explain, parameters and 7.x–9.0 release notes, plus Compass query/explain/index pages and Atlas performance/query pages. Third-party text; private reading aid; never publish. — file://<local-path> · keywords: index, query optimization, release notes
- [passage] The examples in the following sections use queries against the `sample_mflix.movies` collection in the [sample data](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/import/load-sample-data.md#std-label-sample-data) to illustrate the improvements to flexibility and performance that MongoDB Search offers over [`$text`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/text.md#mongodb-query-op.-text). You can run the queries from both examples using the following indexes: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/recommend-search-text.md#create-the-indexes · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization, sample_mflix.movies, $text
- [passage] You can create a text index to improve the performance of text queries run on a collection containing documents or embedded documents with text in multiple languages. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/specify-language-text-index/create-text-index-multiple-languages.md · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization
- [passage] By default, the `default_language` for text indexes is `english`. To improve the performance of non-English `$text` queries, you can specify a different default language associated with your text index. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/specify-text-index-language.md · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization, default_language, english, $text
- [passage] Index use and performance for `$regex` queries depends on whether the query is case-sensitive or case-insensitive. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/regex.md#index-use · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, query optimization, $regex
- [passage] MongoDB 8.2 removes `profileOperationResourceConsumptionMetrics`. Therefore, code depending on [operationMetrics](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#std-label-executionStats) does not work. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#unsharded-collections · keywords: index, release notes, profileOperationResourceConsumptionMetrics
- [statement] Known issue at FCV 9.0: listIndexes reports collation { locale: 'simple' } for simple-collation indexes (SERVER-89953), so Mongoose syncIndexes() (also Doctrine ODM, Beanie) drops and rebuilds unchanged indexes. Workaround: do not call syncIndexes() at startup, or use Mongoose 9.10.4 / 8.24.5. Fix targeted for a future 9.0 patch. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/release-notes/9.0/ · keywords: index, release notes, Post-8.0 Query Engine Changes (8.1 and 8.2 rapid releases and 9.0)
- [passage] The following example returns the index named `synonym-mappings` on the `movies` collection: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/listSearchIndexes.md#return-a-single-search-index-by-name · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, synonym-mappings, movies
- [passage] 3. Run the [atlas clusters search nodes create](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-clusters-search-nodes-create.md#std-label-atlas-clusters-search-nodes-create) command with the `--file` option. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/reference/json/search-index-config-file.md#create-an-atlas-search-index · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, --file
- [passage] 3. Run the [atlas clusters search nodes update](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-clusters-search-nodes-update.md#std-label-atlas-clusters-search-nodes-update) command with the `--file` option. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/reference/json/search-index-config-file.md#update-an-atlas-search-index · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, --file
- [passage] The `{ "content": "text" }` index only includes the `content` field, and does not return matches on non-indexed fields. For example, the following query searches the `blog` collection for the string `food`: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-text/create-text-index.md#matches-on-non-indexed-fields · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, index, { "content": "text" }, content, blog, food
- [fact] MongoDB documentation recommends rewriting $text-heavy queries as $search to gain flexibility and performance (language awareness, fuzzy matching, highlighting, autocomplete, synonyms, relevance scoring), with the gain growing as data size and query breadth grow. The same page calls $text adequate for simple, narrow searches, so migration is not advised for every query. — https://mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/recommend-search-text · keywords: Atlas Search vs text search, query optimization, Atlas Search vs $text vs $regex (search offload decision)
- [passage] - Deleting many documents can fragment storage files, additionally impacting performance. - [passage] In some cases, the query planner uses a `DISTINCT_SCAN` index plan that returns one document per index key value. `DISTINCT_SCAN` executes faster than `IXSCAN` if there are multiple documents per key value. - [passage] During the `$match` stage, the server can use an index if `$match` is the first stage in the pipeline, after any optimizations from the [query planner.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-plans.md#std-label-query-plans-query-optimization) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/aggregation-pipeline-optimization.md#indexes · keywords: index, query optimization, $match
